Rarity.rationale: Obtainable, and the grant path IS the reachability argument because an Ancient relic is not in the grab bag: `py audit/tools/relic_probes_b18.py b18-pool` reports bag='-' and granted_by=['sts2_rl/events/tezcatara.py'] -- the ported Act-2 Tezcatara ancient offers it as one of OPTION_POOL_1 (events/tezcatara.py:16, offered at events/tezcatara.py:44-48). Rule 7: sts2_rl/events/tezcatara.py is not hashed by this record.

HasUponPickupEffect.rationale: Matches YummyCookie.cs:19 exactly. Worth an entry rather than a tick because the sibling upgrade-on-pickup relic audited in batch 12, relic/pomander, does NOT declare it -- and that is also correct, because Pomander.cs declares no such override (audit/records/relic/pomander.json guard N5 records the same asymmetry from the other side). PROMPT.md bug class 29: sibling relics may differ on purpose; a reviewer who made the family look alike would break one of the two. Its only reader on either side is the tradability test (RelicModel.IsTradable, RelicModel.cs:176-200; relics/base.py:132), and both sides additionally exclude ANCIENT rarity (relics/base.py:134-136), so a Yummy Cookie is untradable for two independent reasons on each side. Rule 7: src/Core/Models/RelicModel.cs, sts2_rl/relics/base.py and audit/records/relic/pomander.json are not hashed by this record.

AfterObtained.rationale: YummyCookie.cs:70-77 selects `DynamicVars.Cards.IntValue` == 4 upgradable deck cards through CardSelectCmd.FromDeckForUpgrade and calls CardCmd.Upgrade on each; yummy_cookie.py:18-21 does the same through run.select_cards('upgrade', run.upgradable_cards(), 4) and card.upgrade(). Every clause maps: the IsUpgradable candidate filter (guard N1, the bug-class-14 / sweep-D check, cleared by execution), the auto-take-when-the-list-is-short semantics (N2), the select-then-mutate ordering (N3) and the constant 4 (N2). EXECUTED (`py audit/tools/relic_probes_b18.py b18-cookie`): a starting deck offers 10 candidates and comes out with exactly 4 cards at upgrade_level 1; a deck of 3 upgradable cards upgrades all 3; a deck of 0 upgrades none. Rollup of N1-N8 per binding rule 4: the worst verdict among them is the presentation/telemetry waiver of N4 and N6, so this hook carries no divergence. Rule 7: src/Core/Commands/CardSelectCmd.cs, src/Core/Commands/CardCmd.cs and sts2_rl/run.py are not hashed by this record.

guards.what: N1 (bug class 14 / sweep D, CLEARED by execution): the sim's Card.upgrade() has no IsUpgradable guard, but Yummy Cookie's candidate list carries it
guards.rationale: C#'s CardCmd.Upgrade skips any card whose IsUpgradable is false (`if (!card.IsUpgradable) continue;`, CardCmd.cs:273-276) and the sim's Card.upgrade() (cards/base.py:146-148) is a bare `upgrade_level += 1` plus _on_upgrade with no guard, so every sim caller must supply its own filter -- the class that fired as a LIVE gap on relic/astrolabe and relic/bone_tea. Yummy Cookie supplies it: run.upgradable_cards() (run.py:368-369) is `[c for c in self.deck if c.is_upgradable]` and Card.is_upgradable (cards/base.py:167-170) is CardModel.IsUpgradable's `CurrentUpgradeLevel < MaxUpgradeLevel`. That mirrors the source, which filters in the same place -- CardSelectCmd.FromDeckForUpgrade takes `PileType.Deck.GetPile(player).Cards.Where(c => c.IsUpgradable)` (CardSelectCmd.cs:442) -- so both sides filter the candidate list and both are safe. EXECUTED (`py audit/tools/relic_probes_b18.py b18-cookie`): a deck carrying curse_of_the_bell and dazed (both max_upgrade_level 0) offers neither as a candidate and leaves both at upgrade_level 0; a Strike already at level 1/1 is likewise excluded and comes out unchanged. THE BATCH BRIEF'S PRE-DIAGNOSIS IS STALE: it says yummy_cookie is in sweep D's unguarded-upgrade list. The CURRENT sweep output puts it under `guarded (for contrast)` alongside pomander, fishing_rod and twelve others, and sweep D's own published correction names yummy_cookie as one of five sites its first 3-line-window version over-reported. Same verdict as audit/records/relic/pomander.json guard N1 and audit/records/relic/fishing_rod.json guard N2 (binding rule 3). Rule 7: src/Core/Commands/CardCmd.cs, src/Core/Commands/CardSelectCmd.cs, sts2_rl/cards/base.py, sts2_rl/run.py, .superpowers/sdd/content-relic-sweeps.md and the two sibling records are not hashed by this record.

guards.what: N2: `CardSelectorPrefs(UpgradeSelectionPrompt, DynamicVars.Cards.IntValue)` with CardsVar(4) (YummyCookie.cs:62, :72) vs `run.select_cards('upgrade', candidates, 4)` (yummy_cookie.py:16, :20)
guards.rationale: The two-argument CardSelectorPrefs constructor sets MinSelect = MaxSelect = selectCount and therefore RequireManualConfirmation = false (CardSelectorPrefs.cs:62-78), so FromDeckForUpgrade's `if (list.Count <= prefs.MinSelect && !prefs.RequireManualConfirmation) enumerable = list;` (CardSelectCmd.cs:448-451) auto-takes the whole list when the deck has four or fewer upgradable cards, and its `if (list.Count == 0) return Array.Empty` (CardSelectCmd.cs:443-446) handles none. RunState.select_cards clamps identically with `count = min(count, len(candidates))` and returns [] for an empty candidate list (run.py:384-386). CardsVar(4) read as IntValue is the pinned non-ascension value -- there is no AscensionHelper.GetValueIfAscension anywhere in YummyCookie.cs -- and the sim's CARDS = 4 matches; checked against the C# and not against the port's docstring, per PROMPT.md bug class 19. EXECUTED (`b18-cookie`): decks of 4 / 3 / 1 / 0 upgradable cards upgrade 4 / 3 / 1 / 0 of them, each to level 1. WHICH cards are chosen is a player decision on both sides (the sim delegates to run.card_selector and falls back to a uniform run-RNG sample, run.py:387-390), so the selection itself is not a fidelity question -- but see N7 for the one property of it that is. Same verdict as audit/records/relic/pomander.json guard N2 (binding rule 3). Rule 7: src/Core/CardSelection/CardSelectorPrefs.cs, src/Core/Commands/CardSelectCmd.cs, sts2_rl/run.py and audit/records/relic/pomander.json are not hashed by this record.

guards.what: N3: `CardCmd.Upgrade(item)` is called per selected card in a loop after the WHOLE selection resolves (YummyCookie.cs:72-76); the sim upgrades inside the for-loop over the returned list (yummy_cookie.py:20-21)
guards.rationale: Same structure -- select first, then upgrade the returned set. This matters more here than at the single-card sites because 4 cards are picked at once: if the selection were interleaved with the upgrades, an early upgrade could take a card to max level and remove it from the still-open candidate list. Both sides materialise the selection before mutating -- C# with `.ToList()` at YummyCookie.cs:72, the sim because run.select_cards returns a list -- so the candidate set is the pre-upgrade one on both. Same verdict as audit/records/relic/pomander.json guard N3 (binding rule 3), where the single-card case made it unobservable; here it is the real thing and it holds. Rule 7: audit/records/relic/pomander.json is not hashed by this record.

guards.what: N4: CardCmd.Upgrade's other two side effects -- the `if (CombatManager.Instance.IsEnding) return;` early bail (CardCmd.cs:265-270) and the `CurrentMapPointHistoryEntry...UpgradedCards.Add(card.Id)` bookkeeping (CardCmd.cs:277-281)
guards.rationale: The IsEnding return is a mid-combat-teardown guard and AfterObtained is an out-of-combat pickup, so it cannot be reached; UpgradedCards is the game's own save/replay bookkeeping, which the sim's conformance layer READS out of the save (as the oracle) rather than writes. Neither can change a game state either codebase can observe. Waived under the presentation/out-of-scope-machinery exclusion rather than on an unreachability claim about ported content -- the same verdict and the same basis as audit/records/relic/neows_talisman.json guard N3 (binding rule 3). Rule 7: src/Core/Commands/CardCmd.cs and audit/records/relic/neows_talisman.json are not hashed by this record.

guards.what: N5: `card.UpgradeInternal(); card.FinalizeUpgradeInternal();` (CardCmd.cs:283-284) vs the sim's `upgrade_level += 1; self._on_upgrade()` (cards/base.py:146-148)
guards.rationale: This is the shared card-layer upgrade mechanism, not something this relic does differently: the port calls the same Card.upgrade() that every other ported upgrader calls, so any divergence in it belongs to cards/base.py and is one verdict for the whole codebase (binding rule 3), already carried at audit/records/relic/pomander.json guard N1 and audit/records/relic/fishing_rod.json guard N2. Recorded here only to state that this relic adds nothing of its own between the selection and the upgrade -- the port's body is three lines and there is no extra effect on either side (YummyCookie.cs has no Flash(), no counter and no second command). Rule 7: src/Core/Commands/CardCmd.cs, sts2_rl/cards/base.py and the two sibling records are not hashed by this record.

guards.what: N6: `IconBaseName` (YummyCookie.cs:21-60) picks a per-character icon and, on the canonical/ownerless instance, does so with `Rng.Chaotic.NextItem(ModelDb.AllCharacters)` cached in a STATIC field; plus `AfterCloned` -> `RelicIconChanged()` (YummyCookie.cs:64-68)
guards.rationale: Both are presentation -- which of the five character-flavoured cookie sprites the relic bar shows, and an icon refresh after a model clone. The sim has no relic UI. Waived under the shared contract's presentation/animation exclusion. The reason this needed thought rather than a tick is the RNG draw: PROMPT.md bug class 16's second half is about named RNG streams a port silently reroutes, so a `Rng.…NextItem` inside a relic is worth checking even in an icon getter. It cannot matter: `Rng.Chaotic` is `new Rng((uint)DateTimeOffset.Now.ToUnixTimeSeconds())` (src/Core/Random/Rng.cs:22) -- a wall-clock-seeded stream that is not part of the run's deterministic state at all, is not in RunRngSet/PlayerRngSet, and is drawn from once per process into a static cache. So there is no stream position for the sim to keep in parity, and this is the opposite of the astrolabe/fishing_rod case where a named per-run stream was at stake. `CanonicalVars`' CardsVar(4) is presentation for the description text; its VALUE is verdicted in N2, not waived here. Rule 7: src/Core/Random/Rng.cs is not hashed by this record.

guards.what: N7 (residual, not a divergence): run.select_cards does not de-duplicate and Card.upgrade() does not clamp, so a card_selector policy that returned the same card twice would push it PAST max_upgrade_level -- something C#'s selection screen cannot do
guards.rationale: EXECUTED (`py audit/tools/relic_probes_b18.py b18-cookie`, last line): with a deliberately malformed selector returning `[target] * count`, a Strike whose max_upgrade_level is 1 comes out at upgrade_level 4. C# cannot reach that state -- FromDeckForUpgrade returns either the filtered list itself or a set of distinct cards from NDeckUpgradeSelectScreen / Selector.GetSelectedCards (CardSelectCmd.cs:440-472) -- and CardCmd.Upgrade would re-check IsUpgradable per card anyway (CardCmd.cs:273-276), so a duplicate would be skipped the second time. Verdicted faithful rather than a gap because it is NOT reachable with ported content and rule 6 requires proving reachability, not asserting it: both selector implementations that ship pick distinct cards -- RunDriver._card_selector pops each choice out of `remaining` (driver.py:246-267) and scripted_card_selector slices a sorted enumerate of the candidates (selectors.py:57-83) -- and the no-selector fallback is `self.rng.sample`, which is without replacement (run.py:390). What would make it live is a NEW selector implementation, not new content, which is why it is recorded as a residual here and reported as a latent pool-wide shape in .superpowers/sdd/relic-batch-18-lessons.md rather than filed as a dormant gap. It is worth writing down because the bug-class-14 guard everyone checks (a filtered candidate list) protects against a non-upgradable candidate and NOT against a repeated one, and because the sibling purpose fails LOUDLY where this one fails silently: run.remove_cards calls list.remove and raises on a duplicate (run.py:356-358), while an extra upgrade just silently exceeds the max. Yummy Cookie is the largest such site in the relic pool (CARDS = 4). Rule 7: src/Core/Commands/CardSelectCmd.cs, src/Core/Commands/CardCmd.cs, sts2_rl/run.py, sts2_rl/driver.py and sts2_rl/selectors.py are not hashed by this record.

guards.what: N8: the port implements no `undo_after_obtained`, so the 4 upgrades survive the conformance runner's relic swap
guards.rationale: PROMPT.md v6 binding item 3: the ABSENCE of undo_after_obtained is faithful at every site -- the helper has no C# counterpart (nothing in the game un-picks a relic), so a sim lacking it is not diverging from the source, which is the only question this audit asks; and it is not a waiver either, because there is no source behaviour to be faithful to. The operational consequence still belongs on the record: the conformance runner lets the sim grant a node's relic and then swaps it for the one the save says was really picked (relics/base.py:143-150 states the purpose), and an unwound Yummy Cookie leaves 4 deck cards upgraded, which the runner's `(id, upgrade_level)` deck comparison reads as a parity failure. EXECUTED (`py audit/tools/relic_probes_b18.py b18-cookie-undo`): 0 upgraded cards before, 4 after the pickup, still 4 after undo_after_obtained + removing the relic; the method is confirmed to be the inherited Relic no-op. That is a tooling defect, not a fidelity gap. Note the DISTINCT mechanism v6 flags as a real gap -- an undo_after_obtained that EXISTS and clamps instead of subtracting (mango G1, lees_waffle N4, looming_fruit N3) -- does not apply here, because none exists. Rule 7: sts2_rl/relics/base.py and sts2_rl/conformance/runner.py are not hashed by this record.
